documents.title: The selection rule: precision 1.000 and recall 1.000, with no zero consulted
header: > Locating is not detecting. The spectrum has 149 local maxima in that band and only 30 are ordinates; the rest are ripples of the estimate. A rule is needed, and it must not consult the answer. Two zero-blind signals work, and neither works alone: a true line is a pole of the filter, so it sits still when the estimator is disturbed, whereas a ripple is an artefact of one particular fit. So disturb it two independent ways — change the filter order (five orders, majority vote), and change the mesh entirely (the Δ = 0.015 recursion is a different kernel row, a different recursion and a different band). Nothing but a real line survives both. The rule keeps 30 lines, of which 30 are ordinates: precision 1.000, recall 1.000. And the count is independently predicted: Riemann–von Mangoldt gives N(103.7) = θ(T)/π + 1 = 30.65, which also consults no zero.
- Band: r < 103.7 at mesh Δ = 0.03 (399 nodes); 149 local maxima, of which 30 are true ordinates.

header: **Status:** VERIFIED (numerical, six node sets positive definite by 60-digit Cholesky)
**Source:** [`rh20.html`](../rh20.html) — §4 "The other side of the same ratio"; the certificates are tabulated in Figure 4

> rh18's identity holds at arbitrary real nodes with a single hat width, so a pair supplies more than two separate statements: the union Δ₁ℤ ∪ Δ₂ℤ is itself a legitimate node set, and 𝒲(g⋆ǧ) on hat-splines over that set is a Gram form to be certified. Six of them are, by 60-digit Cholesky, at half-support 11.52 — the certificates are in Figure 4.
The conditioning result stated with it:

> Reduced modulo Δ₁ the union is a single orbit {mθ mod 1}, so its gaps take at most three values — verified in exact rational arithmetic at all six pairs. What separates them is not the count but the balance. The golden pair's three distances are 2.20 + 3.50 + 5.70 (×10⁻³), a ratio of 2.6; a near-rational's are 0.03 + 79.30 + 79.33, a ratio of 2,644. And the certified pivots track the balance exactly: 4.99×10⁻⁶ for the golden pair against 2.76×10⁻⁹ for the near-rational, a factor of 1,810.

documents.title: The instrument — inertia bisection for every λ<sub>min</sub>, cross-checked in 60-digit arithmetic
documents.raw_status: ** VERIFIED (numerical; cross-checked in exact 60-digit decimal arithmetic and by an independent dense exact Cholesky. The method's correctness rests on Sylvester's law of inertia, CITED (literature))
documents.source_line: ** [`rh22.html`](../rh22.html) — §3 "Two traps, and the instrument", paragraph "The instrument"
header: **Status:** VERIFIED (numerical; cross-checked in exact 60-digit decimal arithmetic and by an independent dense exact Cholesky. The method's correctness rests on Sylvester's law of inertia, CITED (literature))
**Source:** [`rh22.html`](../rh22.html) — §3 "Two traps, and the instrument", paragraph "The instrument"

> Every λ<sub>min</sub> in this document is computed by bisection on the *inertia*. By Sylvester's law the number of non-positive Durbin pivots of T − σI is the number of eigenvalues at or below σ, whatever their signs; bisecting on that count has no breakdown mode. It costs O(n²) per test and about seventy tests, which is cheaper than the inverse iteration it replaces. Each reported value is then re-derived in exact 60-digit decimal arithmetic — the two agree to 10<sup>−8</sup> relative at every section size, including the one whose λ<sub>min</sub> is 1.558×10<sup>-10</sup> — and positive-definiteness is confirmed independently by a dense exact Cholesky that shares no code with the Durbin recursion. The bottom eigenvector, which the search needs, is found by inverse iteration on T − σI with σ just *below* λ<sub>min</sub>, which makes the shifted matrix positive definite so that a plain Cholesky applies and nothing is ever divided by an indefinite pivot.
- T is a Toeplitz section; σ is the bisection shift; T − σI is shifted.

documents.title: Trap 2 — the Levinson lie: inverse iteration calls an indefinite section positive
documents.raw_status: ** VERIFIED (numerical) — the failure of the method is exhibited, not a theorem
documents.source_line: ** [`rh22.html`](../rh22.html) — §3 "Two traps, and the instrument", paragraph "Trap 2 · the Levinson lie"
header: **Status:** VERIFIED (numerical) — the failure of the method is exhibited, not a theorem
**Source:** [`rh22.html`](../rh22.html) — §3 "Two traps, and the instrument", paragraph "Trap 2 · the Levinson lie"

> That would have been caught immediately if λ<sub>min</sub> had been computed honestly. rh19–rh21 computed it by inverse iteration through the Levinson–Durbin recursion, which is fast and exact-enough on a positive-definite Toeplitz row. On an *indefinite* one it divides by β<sub>k</sub> = det<sub>k</sub>/det<sub>k−1</sub>, which has changed sign, and what comes out has no relation to the spectrum. Here it comes out **positive**, at 7.114×10<sup>-9</sup> — for a matrix whose smallest eigenvalue is -1.8681. And it is worse than a wrong number: 7.114×10<sup>-9</sup> is within 43% of the *correct* section's 4.990×10<sup>-9</sup>, so it survives every order-of-magnitude sanity check a reader would apply. It is not the first time in this arc that a float lane has been caught lying about an indefinite section. It is the first time the lie was plausible.
- The Levinson–Durbin recursion computes λ<sub>min</sub> by inverse iteration; it divides by β<sub>k</sub> = det<sub>k</sub>/det<sub>k−1</sub>.

documents.title: The weight at the zeros — the searched optimum reaches a geometric-mean weight of 1.138×10<sup>-2</sup>, 1691× the hat
documents.source_line: ** [`rh22.html`](../rh22.html) — §6 "The certificate, and what the gain buys", paragraph "The weight at the zeros"
header: **Source:** [`rh22.html`](../rh22.html) — §6 "The certificate, and what the gain buys", paragraph "The weight at the zeros"

> Scored on rh21's own statistic — the geometric mean of |ĥ(γ)|² over the first forty zeros at unit energy — the hat gives 6.729×10<sup>-6</sup>, rh21's Slepian in this family 1.615×10<sup>-4</sup>, and the optimum 1.138×10<sup>-2</sup>: a factor 1691 over the hat, against the 62× rh21 measured for a continuous Slepian. rh21's barrier w ≤ πC(0)/T = 2.5552×10<sup>-2</sup> still holds, as it must for every compactly supported window, but the room under it has almost gone: the hat sat 3797× under, rh21's Slepian 158×, the optimum 2.25×.
- |ĥ(γ)|² is the squared transform of the window at the zero height γ; the statistic is the geometric mean over the first forty zeros at unit energy.

documents.title: Which half binds
header: > This is the part worth having. For the triangle hat the even block binds at all nine section sizes tested, from n = 9 to n = 76, and never narrowly: the odd block is between 2.65× and 34.9× above it. For every one of the four searched windows the two blocks are within 26%, they agree to 0.14% at the deepest section, and *which* one binds alternates with n — the sign pattern over the nine sizes is O O O E E O E O O for the searched M = 16 spline and O E O E E O O O O for the notch-free one.

> The practical one is negative and should be said plainly: neither channel can be certified on its own. A certificate that establishes positivity of the cosine block at every n proves nothing, because at some n the sine block is the smaller. The split is a factor, not a reduction.
